question:
Batch 71 = RULING 84 (orchestrator 2026-11-13 '20:40'), verbatim: "My ruling 72 was too narrow. (a) FILLERS the second recogniser hears and Whisper drops (um, uh, er, ah, mm, hmm) are in the adopt class with the speaker's own repetitions: the lock takes the spoken text, verdicts carry over, G18 compares against it. (b) ONE function-word disagreement between the two recognisers in a span (so / or, a / the, in / on) is the 'one ambiguous token' already ruled acceptable with acoustic identity (numbers, names, negations and content words always hold); the lock keeps the render decode's word and records the other reading. Two or more such disagreements in one span still hold. This is in your pre-check service (and wherever adjudicate_lock classes differences)."
Context: lock_precheck.py (the pin-stage pre-check) compares the lock with the second recogniser (Scribe) on every span (ruling 72); an adoption puts the spoken text through the render's own segment_lock/adjudicate_lock (pinned.py). adjudicate_lock (ruling 17/18) compares the render decode (r) with the approved text (p); Scribe decides. Ruling 18's record ("alternatives": token_index into the lock text's canon tokens, readings, word_index, source_span) is what G18 (word_diff.py, unchanged) accepts at one token with the acoustic check; G18 refuses more than one alternative per lock; G18 decides omissions (a filler the final's Whisper drops) acoustically (ruling 22).
The change:
- pinned.py: FUNCTION_WORDS moved here unchanged from lock_precheck; FILLERS = exactly the six; one_function_word(x, y); _with_token(text, k, tok) (the word carrying canon token k re-spelled tok, its punctuation/initial capital kept, verified by canon tokens, else None = hold); adjudicate_lock: AFTER the existing "not pin_side -> hold", a ruling 84 (b) branch: ops whose decode side is one token and whose approved side, fillers aside, is one token, both function words. Two or more -> PinError. One -> lock text = run text when that is the only difference, else the approved text with that word re-spelled to the decode's; the other differences recorded as ruling 17's adjudication; the token recorded as alternatives (ruling 18's shape, token_index in the NEW text). Ruling 17 (content words) and ruling 18's branch are unchanged.
- lock_precheck.py: RULES += "ruling 84"; reading() factored out of as_spoken unchanged; ruling84_class per difference: only-Scribe-side fillers -> "filler"; a critical token -> hold; both sides non-empty after fillers -> ONE_FW if one_function_word else hold; else ruling 67's carry_class (unchanged) on the reading without fillers. Adopt iff no hold and at most one ONE_FW. spoken_text stays Scribe's text (so the render's adjudicate_lock sees the function-word difference and records it). Entries gain "alternatives" and as_spoken "classes"; the hold reason names the holding differences.
MEASURED (real cached decode + reading, no GPU, no paid call; tests in test_lock_precheck.TestRuling84MustFail): span 6058ee58 (uaHNzi-Kgr8 153.25-165.89): old classes [um None, uh None, so/or function word] = HOLD (the live service held it 01:28:05Z); new [filler, filler, one function word] = adopt; the render's lock keeps 'so' (token 21, word 63, 22.90-23.12 s) and records 'or', adjudication [um, uh]. 1b4a63d0's hook: HOLD before and after, same classes (when/and immediate repetition, 'the why' function word; "market is"/"market's", "that's why the bull that's", "w and" hold). Protected references' locks: none has a pin_side function-word substitution (their adjudications: one insert 'dollars'; ruling 18 'think'/'mean' unchanged). Tests: 100 passed; the new ones fail on the old code.
FIND: a path where (b) passes two or more function-word disagreements, a content word, a number/name/negation, or a non-filler word as a filler; a lock whose alternatives token_index does not point at the decode's word in the lock text (G18 would then misread it); a change to ruling 17's or 18's existing outcomes beyond the 1-for-1 function-word case; anything that fails open. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

rejected_findings.issue: The `token_index` recorded in `alternatives` points to the position in the second recogniser's token list (`p`), not the lock text's canonical tokens. G18 expects `token_index` to index into the lock text's canon tokens. If the lock text differs from the second recogniser's text by more than just the function word (e.g., due to fillers or other differences), the index will be incorrect, causing G18 to misread the alternative.
rejected_findings.fix: Compute the token index in the new lock text's canonical tokens, not in `p`.

rejected_findings.issue: The `word_index` is computed using `_token_word(words, lock["i0"], lock["i1"], a)`, where `a` is the index in the run decode's token list (`r`). However, the lock text may have been modified (e.g., by ruling 17's adoption of the approved text), so the word index in the original `words` list may not correspond to the correct word in the new lock text. This could lead to an incorrect `source_span`.
rejected_findings.evidence: text, wi = run_t if n == r else _with_token(pin_t, c, r[a]), _token_word(words, lock["i0"], lock["i1"], a)
rejected_findings.fix: Ensure the word index is computed relative to the new lock text's words, not the original run decode's words.

rejected_findings.issue: In the ruling 84 (b) branch, when the second recogniser's reading equals the run decode except for the one function word (n == r), the lock text becomes run_t but the recorded adjudication is skipped (kept == []), so the lock carries 'alternatives' with no 'adjudication' — yet the branch's own docstring and the ruling say every other difference is ruling 17's; more importantly the kept-differences computation runs SequenceMatcher(r, n) where n = p[:c] + [r[a]] + p[c+1:], i.e. the approved side with the decode's word substituted, so any *other* difference (e.g. a filler the second recogniser heard) is recorded as ruling 17's adjudication with the decode's word already in the approved side — but the lock text in that case is _with_token(pin_t, c, r[a]), the approved text re-spelled, so the recorded differences' left side (' '.join(r[a2:b2])) is the run decode's tokens, not the new lock text's, and G18's word_diff against the new lock text would see those as differences unless it re-derives them; the test only covers the case where the sole other differences are fillers (deletions), where left side is ''.
rejected_findings.evidence: kept = [[" ".join(r[a2:b2]), " ".join(n[c2:d2])] for op, a2, b2, c2, d2 in SequenceMatcher(None, r, n, autojunk=False).get_opcodes() if op != "equal"]
rejected_findings.fix: Compute kept against the new lock text's canon tokens (canon_tokens(text)) rather than r, or assert text's tokens == r when kept is non-empty; otherwise a non-filler second difference (e.g. a content word) recorded in adjudication would not match the new lock text G18 compares against.
